done_when: On Windows, a builder's own test run skips each separate browser-test step and prints one line saying so, while the pull request check, the final check and the full test run still run them, Mac and Linux runs stay the same, and a test setting that is one combined script still runs whole.

known.title: Functional: Preserve non-browser checks when identifying browser steps
Not done: Windows builder runs do not skip every separate browser-test step
Gate: restore the historical guide fixtures
Not done: Windows browser-test steps are classified incorrectly
Gate: Restore the historical fixture guides

findings.body:
chunk 1/3:

Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A Windows repo uses Forge's default Node test setting, with `pretest` running unit tests or lint and `test` running `playwright test`. This lookup inspects only the `test` script, so Forge removes the entire `npm test` invocation and runs neither `pretest` nor `posttest`; it can report success after only `npm ci`. npm runs those lifecycle scripts as part of `npm test` ([npm scripts documentation](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/using-npm/scripts/#life-cycle-operation-order)). The invocation must remain whole when it also runs non-browser checks.
findings.title: Functional: Preserve non-browser checks when identifying browser steps

findings.body:
chunk 1/3:

Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - A Windows workspace runs `npm exec --workspace apps/web -- playwright test`. The classifier treats `apps/web`, the value of the workspace option, as an unrelated program and returns false before reaching Playwright. The same happens for `npx --package=@playwright/test -- playwright test`, because splitting the option at `/` produces `test`. These are supported npm launcher forms ([npm exec documentation](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/commands/npm-exec/)), but Forge runs the browser step and prints no skip notice.
findings.title: Not done: Windows builder runs do not skip every separate browser-test step

findings.body:
chunk 3/3:

Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a Windows repo sets its test command to one combined script, such as `npm run ci`, that runs unit tests and Playwright together. The revised test runs that script only as part of `ALL`, which also contains separate browser steps to remove. Every Windows builder case has at least one removable browser step; none checks the promised single combined setting when there is nothing to skip. That setting takes the no-skip return in `src/forge/fasttest.py:276–277`, so a regression that drops a lone combined npm command could pass this proof while running none of its checks. Add a case with only the combined script and assert that both steps run without a skip notice.
findings.title: Gate: test_3_windows_builder_run_skips_browser_tests_and_nothing_else

stop.reason: The owner chose one more round: repair all three findings

why: On a Windows laptop, a builder's own test run can take up to 24 minutes (a client team reports this; Forge did not measure it), and its browser test steps (Playwright or Cypress) fail there for reasons unrelated to the change, which costs builders time and rounds.
